idea: An app where campus event organizers post leftover food and students get notified to come grab it. Two of us, part-time (~12h/week each), 8 weeks, $300 budget. Must be free for students. Want a live map and push notifications.

nodes.label: Organizers post leftover food (photo, location, pickup window)
nodes.rationale: Must-have: the supply side of the app

nodes.label: Student feed of available food
nodes.rationale: Students need one place to see what's available now

nodes.label: Push notifications for new food posts
nodes.rationale: Must-have: food goes fast, so students need to know immediately

nodes.label: SMS alerts for students without the app
nodes.rationale: Reaches students who won't install an app

objections.reason: ~$250 in SMS fees alone breaks the $300 budget
Collecting phone numbers adds privacy obligations

nodes.label: Live map of food locations
nodes.rationale: User asked for it; makes finding food in unfamiliar buildings easy

objections.reason: 30h is over a fifth of total capacity for something a building name already solves
Unvalidated that students need a map rather than a building and room

nodes.label: Building and room shown as text, with a link to campus maps
nodes.rationale: Smaller variant of the live map: most of the value for 2h

nodes.label: Claim / reserve a portion
nodes.rationale: Prevents wasted trips when food is gone

objections.reason: Reservation state and no-shows add 14h of edge cases
Organizers may not want to manage reservations

nodes.label: In-app chat between organizers and students
nodes.rationale: Questions like 'is there any vegan food left?'

nodes.label: Campus email sign-in
nodes.rationale: Keeps the app to the campus community and deters abuse

nodes.label: Allergen and dietary labels required on every post
nodes.rationale: Students with allergies must be able to decide safely

nodes.label: Food-safety liability (time since prepared, handling)
nodes.rationale: Posting checklist plus a pickup-window limit and disclaimer

nodes.label: Students may not trust food from strangers
nodes.rationale: Show the posting organization's name and verified campus email

evidence.title: Consumer food waste behaviour in universities: Sharing as a means of prevention
evidence.summary: A campus food-sharing intervention ran into barriers: trust, people's visceral relationship with food, and norms about acceptable food sources.

questions.question: Which campus organizations would post food first?
questions.why: Without reliable posters there is nothing for students to find

questions.question: Is a mobile-friendly web app OK, or do you need native iOS/Android apps?
questions.why: Native apps roughly double the frontend work and add app-store review time
questions.answer: Mobile web is fine to start

questions.question: The agents disagree on 'Live map of food locations'. Build it now, defer it, or drop it?
questions.why: Supported by architect. Objections: delivery: 30h is over a fifth of total capacity; evidence: unvalidated need

tasks.title: Post form with allergen labels and safety checklist

agents.name: Food Safety & Liability Specialist
agents.reason: Idea involves distributing food to the public; highest-ranked regulatory_review specialist

negotiation.message: The live map and SMS reach are what make this better than a group chat. Keep both.
138h planned against 134h capacity, and SMS alone costs $250 of a $300 budget. Reject.
Allergen labels and a food-safety checklist must be on every post before anything else ships.
r1-delivery: Drop SMS, defer chat and claiming, replace the live map with building and room text.
negotiation.counteroffer: Drop SMS, defer chat and claiming, replace the live map with building and room text.

negotiation.message: On r1-delivery: Dropping SMS is fair given the budget, but the map is the main reason students would use this over a group chat.
On r1-delivery: Fits with 30h of buffer and $60 of spend.
On r1-delivery: Accept; no evidence the map matters more than reliable posters.
No candidate was accepted by everyone. r1-delivery has the most support (2/3) and becomes the draft for the next round.
